claims.statement: For a finite integer-complex CRN with density-dependent falling-factorial propensities, a compact positive relative polytope Q, a lattice-compatible buffered initial count, bounded predictable rates k_t in a supplied state-dependent compact allocation set K(X_t), and a strict facet collar margin sup_{x in collar_i,k in K(x)} sum_r k_r x^{y_r}(exp(-theta_i a_i dot nu_r)-1) <= -eta_i, the stopped exit probability obeys the explicit N35-type bound with the exact O(1/V) factorial correction. The result is finite-horizon and uniform over the admissible predictable controls.
assumptions: supplied exact propensity convention and bounded rates
supplied compact positive polytope and collars
supplied joint rate allocation set K(x)
strict exponential-generator margin on every collar
claims.novelty_boundary: The exponential-supermartingale, CTMDP, and finite-volume safety ingredients are established; this is a coupled-rate interface refinement of the supplied N35 proof. No novelty claim is made.
costs: feed, fuel, turnover and controller costs over horizon
simulation event activity O(V Lambda T)
claims.falsifier: A feasible measured (x,k) in a certified collar violates the stated MGF margin, or an exact/valid replicated exit estimate exceeds the bound under the complete model contract.
claims.next_gate: Acquire one real closed or explicitly budgeted metabolic subnetwork and measured K(x), certify all collars, then compare against same-information independent-box and finite-state CTMDP baselines.

claims.statement: In the stipulated two-reaction model 2A->A+B and 2B->A+B on A+B=V, the coupled allocation k_A=k_B=q in [1,16] has inward collar margin 7/16 on Q=[1/4,3/4]. A rational exponential certificate gives theta=1/2, eta=3/20, V0=223 and, at V=3000, exit probability below 2.16877191e-6 through T=exp(23.4375). Replacing the coupled set by [1,16]^2 fails at x=1/4,k_A=16,k_B=1 with drift -7/16.
assumptions: stipulated normalized rates and tied allocation; no biological measurements
claims.novelty_boundary: A worked application of SM-01; no claim that these rates or this rate coupling occur in a biological system.
costs: exact thinning upper cost approximately 4.53e14 candidate events per run at the stated horizon
claims.falsifier: Any feasible rate allocation or collar state violates the certified margin; a physical test also requires measured rate-set membership and model-error control.
claims.next_gate: Add an exact-rational verifier and run a small-volume Bellman comparator before any biological interpretation.

claims.statement: In the N35 finite-horizon proof, the factorial correction D_i and projected quadratic jump constant Q_i may use a certified coordinate box U^i containing only facet i's collar; the global total hazard Lambda still uses a box for all of Q. This preserves the same exit-bound proof and can improve V0 and the exponent.
assumptions: same N35 integer-complex, propensity, collar, and lattice-start contract
valid certified collar-specific coordinate upper bounds
claims.novelty_boundary: A direct localization of N35's supplied proof constants; not claimed as a new large-deviation principle.
costs: global event hazard and stopped simulation remain charged
claims.falsifier: A count-lattice state in a collar violates its local factorial or quadratic bound, or a valid run violates the resulting exit bound.
claims.next_gate: Compare with the joint-rate support-function theorem on measured coupled fluxes.

claims.statement: Conditional on the N33 candidate theorem for an integer-complex all-endotactic network and fixed positive rate box, its finite affine plateau is a compact relative polytope. The weighted facet drift and continuity over the compact facet-rate product imply a strictly inward collar on each proper relative facet; hence N35 applies once an effective certificate and buffered lattice start are acquired.
assumptions: finite affine family and compact plateau
lattice-compatible count start at the selected volume
claims.novelty_boundary: The deterministic theorem is a source-derived all-dimensional candidate; two-species time-varying permanence is established prior art. The bridge yields existence, not computable margins or a practical compiler.
costs: affine family size/precision and scale have no useful bound
collar widths and margins are nonconstructive
molecular rate/lattice data must be supplied
claims.falsifier: A valid candidate network/facet/rate vector contradicts the weighted drift, or a valid mass-action CTMC contradicts the N35 finite-horizon bound after the collar is certified.
claims.next_gate: Independent external proof review of N33 and a named-network certificate with exact bit-size/acquisition accounting.

claims.statement: For the four-pair open internal CRN 2C<->A+B+C, A+B+C<->3A+2B, 3A+2B<->2C, 2C<->2C+D with all effective rates one, the deterministic system is detailed balanced at (1,1,1,1) in B+C=2. For every integer n>=0, the falling-factorial CTMC has a closed irreducible positive-recurrent class Gamma_n={(n,0,2,d),(n+1,1,1,d),(n+3,2,0,d):d>=0}; its stationary law is the unit product-Poisson law restricted to Gamma_n, so A>=n and the family is not tight across classes.
assumptions: open internal subsystem with chemostatted balancing species Q at fixed activity 1
all four reaction pairs reversible with unit effective rates
unit-volume falling-factorial propensities; a fixed-V scaling is separately derived in stochastic_safety/OBSTRUCTION.md
claims.novelty_boundary: A reversible completion of source-reported U/N77. Established global-attractor and ACK product-form theorems supply the general machinery; exact construction priority is unverified. This does not refute componentwise positive recurrence or fixed-interior fluid limits.
costs: high-order reaction channels require physical calibration
stationary sampling rare phase is O(n^3) observations asymptotically and high turnover is Theta(n^3)
claims.falsifier: Under the calibrated exact propensity model, any forbidden transition, stationary sample with A<n, or phase flux mismatch falsifies this realization.
claims.next_gate: Search exact-network prior art, test a lower-order chemically realizable analogue, and independently verify all communicating classes and stationary balance.

claims.statement: The pinned P/N33 candidate claims that every finite all-endotactic actual-power-law diagram with uniformly positive bounded measurable rate paths has one compact convex positive absorber in each positive stoichiometric class, with finite entry time independent of the rate path.
claims.novelty_boundary: The 2010 CNP theorem already proves the two-species time-varying case. Potential boundary is arbitrary dimension; no external proof or priority clearance.
costs: affine coefficients and scale are nonconstructive
no useful bit-height or entry-time bound
claims.falsifier: An exact endotactic finite diagram and allowed measurable rate path with a positive-class trajectory violating the common compact absorber/entry claim.
claims.next_gate: External proof review; formalize rational certificates for one named biochemical network.

claims.statement: For the caption-parameterized periodic Monod chemostat example, finite RK4 scans identify an additional species-2-only candidate boundary community at amplitude 0.3 and a conflict between the paper's beta_2 caption/body signs; its omitted species-1 invasion is positive, so the discrepancy does not overturn the permanence conclusion.
claims.novelty_boundary: A reproduction/discrepancy audit, not a theorem refutation or a novel coexistence result.
claims.falsifier: A validated reconstruction of all relevant boundary supports that removes the candidate or resolves the beta_2 transcription conflict.
claims.next_gate: Recheck against the 1998 primary source and certify all boundary invasion signs with interval methods.

claims.statement: For E_dot=p-gamma E with p<=pbar, gamma>=gammabar>=0, and kcat<=kbar, E(t) is bounded by the variation-of-constants envelope and integrated reaction flux by the integral of kbar times that envelope. In a constant-synthesis example, transient average flux is exactly V_FBA[1-(1-exp(-gamma T))/(gamma T)] from zero enzyme reserve.
assumptions: measurable nonnegative p, gamma with supplied envelopes
claims.status: elementary_internal_derivation; broad transient gap covered by deFBA/r-deFBA prior art
claims.novelty_boundary: Useful audit lemma, not a new dynamic-FBA framework.
claims.falsifier: Measured flux integral has a valid lower confidence bound above the certificate's upper envelope.
claims.next_gate: Compare against equally informed deFBA/r-deFBA on held-out transients.

claims.statement: Without a supplied maximum reaction order or high-count intervention, no finite low-count passive observation design uniformly identifies global reaction behavior: immigration-death and a hidden higher-order autocatalytic model can have identical generators below the threshold while the latter has explosive high-count dynamics.
assumptions: passive trajectories remain below hidden threshold with high probability
finite number q of trajectories and horizon T
claims.novelty_boundary: Identifiability with a supplied finite order bound and exact rate map is established prior art; this is a finite-observation impossibility boundary.
costs: order bound or high-count intervention acquisition
claims.falsifier: A finite passive procedure with uniform guarantee over every reaction order contradicts the exact below-threshold generator equality bound.
claims.next_gate: Specify an experimentally defensible order bound and identify actual transition rates.
